---
title: "Grades based on standardized evidence"
subtitle: "3.3 · a constructed comparator after the postrank theory book, ch. 2 and 17"
description: "How estimates and standard errors determine evidence flags and the directions they imply."
---

An evidence flag depends on how far an estimate is from a reference in standard error units. Here the rule uses
$z_i = (\hat{\theta}_i-r)/SE_i$ with the reference r set to zero. Values above the upper cutoff receive the highest
flag, and values below the lower cutoff receive the lowest. The remaining values receive the middle flag. If
the flags are treated as grades, a smaller but more precise estimate can rank above a larger one. The two normal
posterior specifications give different assessments of the direction these flags report.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Two units, flat prior.** A has z = 4.00 and B has z = 1.50. The flags state A above B, although B's estimate
  is larger. When each true value has a normal posterior centered on its estimate with SD equal to its SE, this direction
  has error probability .686 and risk .6862. The reversal comes from the difference in standard errors.
- **Same flags, teaching prior.** The error falls to .288; the posterior means are .180 for A and .108 for B.
  The estimates and SEs still give the same flags. The new posterior assigns a lower probability to an error in their direction.
- **B’s SE .15.** B reaches z = 2.00. Both units now receive the same flag, so the report states 0 pairs and has
  risk .2000. Because the flags match, this report leaves the pair unranked.
- **Cutoff 2.576.** The stricter cutoff separates the flags again. The stated direction has error .736. The estimate and its SE determine the flag. The withholding cost τ enters when we evaluate the report.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Reading the cutoff"}
The cutoffs 1.645, 1.96 and 2.576 are the two-sided 10%, 5% and 1% normal critical values. A flag compares one
unit with the reference. The probability that a stated direction between two units is right comes from the posterior.

This constructed comparator follows the postrank theory book, ch. 17 (the Tennessee
procedure in ch. 2 uses a related index with other cutoffs).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
p <- pnorm((.30-.20)/sqrt(.05^2+.20^2))
x <- postrank::postrank_probabilities(array(c(NA,1-p,p,NA),c(2,2,1),dimnames=list(c("A","B"),c("A","B"),"score")), event="directional_error", zero_ties=TRUE, margin=0, source=list(kind="analytic_reference",description="Two-unit example",conditioning="Independent flat-prior normals"), targets=c(score="True value; larger is higher priority"))
postrank::postrank_evaluate(c(A=1L,B=2L),x,weights=c(score=1),tau=.2)[c("N","E_over_N","primary_risk")]
```
:::

Standalone: [evidence-flags](../../embed/evidence-flags.html), for example `?seB=.15&crit=2.576`.

Related applications: [Standardized-evidence flags in a league](flags-in-the-league.qmd), [The decision for an isolated pair](../grades/one-pair.qmd).
